problem: POMDP-based object search methods either assume object independence (scalable but inaccurate) or need accurate ground-truth object correlation for the test environment, which is often unavailable and causes success to drop sharply.
motivation: Home-assistant robots usually know the locations of static furniture, and target objects tend to lie near related objects. Large real-world datasets already encode such co-occurrence, so it can be used as a zero-shot prior for search without per-environment correlation estimates.
key_idea: Train a GAT-based link-prediction GNN on Visual Genome object co-occurrence, then iteratively pick the known object most likely linked to the target and search around it, updating the graph with newly detected objects.
insight: A relationship prior learned from large-scale real images transfers zero-shot to AI2-THOR (67.36% link accuracy vs 86.66% on VG test), and it beats POMDP baselines that use ground-truth correlation. The COS-POMDP (est) ablation shows that estimated correlations degrade performance sharply, which motivates the external prior. The real-robot failures show a dataset bias: the GNN over-predicts sink/counter as related objects.
method: Graph formulation: nodes are object categories with semantic embeddings; edges are co-occurrence relationships; the robot has a 2D grid map with known static object positions.

GNN link predictor: GAT computes node embeddings, and a predictor head outputs the link probability between two nodes. Trained on Visual Genome, with an edge added when a spatial relationship occurs more than 3 times.

Search loop: predict link probabilities between the target and each known object, search the surroundings of the top-scoring one, add newly detected movable objects and their relations to the graph, and repeat until the target is found or the step limit is hit.

Task planner integration: a goal prediction network (LSTM language encoder, MMF) parses instructions into action, subject and object; a PDDL symbolic planner generates the plan; a search step is inserted for any missing object.
Perception: YOLOv5 in simulation; Detic open-vocabulary detector plus depth for 3D pose on the real Stretch RE2.

setting.backbone: GAT link-prediction GNN (trained from scratch) + LSTM goal predictor + PDDL planner; YOLOv5 / Detic detectors
setting.training_data: Visual Genome (>100k images) for the GNN; 8163 explicit instructions from the Symbolic Goal Learning Dataset for the language model
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with object detection; known 2D grid map with static object positions
setting.action_space: low-level MoveAhead 0.25 m / RotateLeft / RotateRight 45°, plus manipulation primitives (Pick, Put, Toggle, Slice, Cook)
setting.privileged: known locations of stationary objects (furniture/fixtures) on a 2D grid map

numbers.backbone: GAT GNN trained on Visual Genome + YOLOv5
numbers.extra: known static object locations; same step budget as baselines; success within 1.0 m

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; the split is not named in the paper, so 'test' is assumed. Also reported: link prediction accuracy of 86.66% (VG test) and 67.36% (AI2-THOR); instruction following Nav/Exe in kitchens: Cook 47.5/42.5, Clean 62.5/62.5, Cut 55.0/20.0, Pick-and-Place 47.5/45.0; real robot search 6/10.
results: GNN-Nav beats COS-POMDP (ground-truth correlation) in all four room types, e.g. bathroom SR 86.67 vs 55.17 and SPL 56.62 vs 30.64, and it far exceeds COS-POMDP (est). Real-robot object search succeeded 6/10, pick-and-place 3/4 and clean 3/4.
limitations: The GNN inherits Visual Genome bias (over-predicts sink/counter), causing real-world search failures.
Manipulation and grasping are weak: the system cannot open containers to search, and grasps slip.
Requires known static object positions and a 2D map; the task planner needs explicit instructions; the real-world evaluation is small (10 search trials, 4 trials per task).
builds_on: Symbolic Goal Learning hybrid task planner (SGL)
